problem: Data collection for embodied navigation and VLN tasks has required custom-built annotation tools each time, and existing tools lack support for voice annotation, pose tracking, and alignment between language and visual percepts/actions.
motivation: High-quality 3D captures have driven navigation datasets, but collection pipelines are ad hoc and costly. A reusable toolkit with speech, pose-trace recording and automatic alignment would speed collection and enable fine-grained spatio-temporal grounding, as needed for the 20,000-hour RxR effort.
key_idea: An open-source, web-based annotation toolkit for panoramic navigation graphs that records speech and virtual camera pose traces and time-aligns transcripts to poses via DTW.
insight: Aligning a manual transcript with a timestamped ASR transcript via dynamic time warping gives fine-grained synchronization between words, pixels seen and actions taken. The paper reports RxR collection lessons: annotators may draft text offline and read it aloud, breaking alignment and changing language (more connectives), which explicit training fixed. Transcription took 3-4x longer than recording speech, which argues for speech-based annotation. No quantitative ablations are given.
method: Panoramic graph environment: assumes discrete navigation graphs over 360° panoramas (Matterport3D, StreetLearn), with actions moving between viewpoints, in a web-based simulation.

Guide task: annotator explores a (optionally path-restricted) environment while recording audio narration, then manually transcribes their own recording; wav upload runs in the background during transcription.
Follower task: annotator listens to the Guide's audio (or reads text) and navigates; audio waveform allows skipping silence or replaying; ends when the Follower stops.
Pose trace recording: timestamped log of the annotator's virtual camera pose, plus the Guide-audio timestamp being heard for Followers.

Transcript-pose alignment utility: Speech-to-Text gives a noisy timestamped transcript, DTW aligns it to the manual transcript, and timestamps propagate to give word-level pose alignment (inspired by Localized Narratives).
Cloud integration and deployment: Firebase storage/database by default; deployment requires a Firebase app, a crowdsourcing platform, and hosted images and graphs.
Best practices and monitoring: annotator training, pilot collections, discarding the first 5-10 annotations, rotating annotators between Guide and Follower, and a dashboard of SR/NE/SPL.

setting.backbone: none (annotation toolkit; uses Google Speech-to-Text and DTW)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views in a web-based simulator (Matterport3D / StreetLearn panoramas)
setting.simulator: custom web-based panoramic graph simulator (Matterport3D / StreetLearn graphs)

numbers_note: No experimental results; this is a toolkit/tools paper. The only quantitative statement is that Guide transcription took 3-4x longer than speech recording.
results: No benchmark results are reported. PanGEA was used to collect Room-Across-Room (20,000+ annotation hours) and for human evaluation of generated instructions in Discriminator21. The main quantitative observation is that transcription cost 3-4x more time than recording speech.
limitations: No guardrails prevent annotators from drafting text offline and reading it aloud, which undermines time alignment; only training addresses this.
Requires discrete panoramic navigation graphs and Firebase/crowdsourcing setup; no continuous environments.
No quantitative evaluation of the toolkit or alignment accuracy.
